about: === GAMEFAQS_GARY: PROFILE FAQ (v2.3) === [1.0] ABOUT: This is a profile. It is also a FAQ. [1.1] AUTHOR: Gary, 18. [1.2] WHAT I DO: I write walkthroughs. Nine are on GameFAQs. Together they are about 300KB of ASCII, which my mom calls 'a lot of typing' and the site calls 'a lot of typing.' [1.3] WHY: Somebody is always stuck in a room and scared of the next one. I'd like them to have a map. [1.4] CORRECTIONS: welcome. Send the section number, the error and a source. You go in the Credits. [1.5] SECTION [4.2b]: a wrong paragraph in v1.04 of my RuneScape guide. Removed in v1.05. If you have v1.04, please update. I am sorry. [1.6] LEGAL: printing this is fine. Framing it is a little much.
aboutMore: [2.0] THINGS NOT IN THE FAQ: [2.1] My mom brings a sandwich at 9 PM and I update the Credits. [2.2] My cousin Danny (7) is my official tester. He can't read yet, so I read each guide aloud, and when he gets bored I cut the section. This is why the guides are good. [2.3] I have never been to a LAN party. Dave invited me. I have prepared a 4-page Attendance Plan. [2.4] I answer every email within 48 hours. Every one.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: whoever wrote the first walkthrough ever (v1.0, probably on a napkin). The editor who rejected v1.0 of my FF7 FAQ for a line-length error (I want to thank them, and also ask about line 41). Dave, at a LAN, with my Attendance Plan. And the person who keeps citing section [4.2b]. I need to know where you found it.

interests.General: writing FAQs (9 on GameFAQs), version control (a folder per version, v1.01 through v1.07), ASCII art, 100% completion runs, tables of contents, line width (79 columns, no exceptions), Ctrl+F, correcting people politely, sandwiches (mom), my cousin Danny (tester, critic)
interests.Music: video game soundtracks (Nobuo Uematsu, Koji Kondo, the Melee menu theme), Radiohead (Everything In Its Right Place is about me and I'm told it isn't), Weezer (the blue album: a document is a document), the Zelda soundtrack on my CD player when I proofread
interests.Movies: WarGames (a kid, a computer, a happy ending), The Princess Bride (the book is better, see [8.2]), Apollo 13 (checklists save lives), Back to the Future (Doc Brown keeps notes), Hackers (I fact-checked it, found 41 errors, filed them)
interests.Television: How It's Made (a proper methodology), Jeopardy (I score myself), Mythbusters, G4's X-Play (I disagree with 14% of the reviews, in writing)
interests.Books: Prima strategy guides (the ones with maps), the Nintendo Power Player's Guide, the Chicago Manual of Style (mom bought it for me), The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (a FAQ for a whole universe, I'm impressed), my own documents (proofread on the bus)
interests.Heroes: the person who wrote the first FAQ ever, the Nintendo Power map-makers, Mr. Henderson (corrects grammar by reflex, I felt seen), my mom (sandwiches), Danny (tester), the dad who emailed me about the Water Temple

bulletins.subject: RULES FOR EMAILING ME (v1.04)
bulletins.body: [1] Check the FAQ first. [2] Check the Table of Contents. [3] Check the Index. [4] If still stuck, send an email. [5] The subject line must include the game and the section. [6] 'help' is not a subject line. [7] I answer within 48 hours. [8] 'You are wrong' is allowed if you cite a source. [9] 'Where is X' see [3.1]. [10] Thank you for reading. I get 14 emails a month. I read all of them. I am not complaining. I am simply pointing out that sections 1 through 3 exist.

My cousin Danny (7) asked me for a guide to level 3-2. I said sure. He said 'can it be short.' I said how short. He said 'the shortest.' It's 6 lines. It's the best thing I've written. v1.0. No errors. Only credit: Danny. I'll keep it.

I found my FF7 FAQ on LimeWire. Labeled 'britney_spears_hit_me.mp3.' 214 downloads. Larry says it's the most popular file in his shared folder. I am trying to be angry. I am also trying to work out what 214 readers is. I think it's my biggest audience ever.
I aligned an ASCII header at 2:58 AM. One space. That is the difference between art and a mistake. I don't expect anyone to notice. That's what makes it correct.

Danny asked me to put sound effects in the Water Temple section. I explained that it's ASCII. He said 'then do it in ASCII.' I've added WHOOSH and SPLASH in 7 places. It's the best section now. I'm credited as the guy who typed it.

blog.title: FAQ: How to Write a FAQ (v1.2)
blog.body: [1] Play the game to 100%. Not 99. [2] Take notes in order. [3] Write the table of contents first. It's a promise. [4] Every section gets a number. If it doesn't have a number it isn't a section, it's a feeling. [5] 79 columns. No exceptions. [6] Test the guide on someone who has never played. For me that's Danny. [7] When Danny gets bored, cut it. [8] Put a Credits section at the end. Longer than you think. [9] Version everything. You will find an error at 3 AM. [10] Remember that on the other end somebody is stuck in a room, scared of the next one, and you've been there. That's [10]. The rest is formatting.

blog.title: Section 4.2b: What Happened (v1.0)
blog.body: In v1.04 of my RuneScape guide there was one paragraph, 4.2b. It said trimmed armor was offered free by friendly players. I got it from a forum post. I did not check it. It was a scam. I found out when Ryan, 14, emailed to say he'd lost his armor, very politely, and that he was still on v1.04 and not mad. I deleted the paragraph that night. That's v1.05. Then I wrote the Scam Guide. Now every document begins: every claim has a source, and when it doesn't, it says so. People still cite 4.2b. Old copies are out there, being wrong in the dark. I don't mind being cited. I mind that I'm not in the room to stop them. So I answer every email. To be continued (v1.1).

blog.title: My Inbox: a retrospective (v1.0)
blog.body: Statistics since v1.0. Emails received: 212. Thank-yous: 190. 'Where is X': 14. 'You are wrong': 7. Of those 7, three were right and I thanked them. Two were rude and I thanked them anyway. Two were Wes. I answer every one within 48 hours. People ask why. It's because the one I can't forget came from a dad whose son was stuck on the Water Temple. They finished it together. He wrote that his boy cheered. I'm 18 and I've never made anyone cheer. I think that's what the 300KB is for. Not the ASCII. Not the version numbers. Somebody sits next to a person who's stuck and says: left, then up, you're nearly there.
